experiment: Stage 2.7 delta-equivalent ordering plus structural exact TT
hypothesis: Replacing full child score recomputation with the proven delta-equivalent ordering calculation lowers the runtime cost of the existing score-order plus structural exact-TT engine without changing its actions, traversal, or cache hits.
interpretation: All 80 tests passed before the benchmark, including exact action, expanded-node, and cache-hit equivalence between the prior score-order + TT engine and the delta-order + TT engine at tested depths.
The delta implementation preserved the prior combined engine's search tree exactly: 882, 2097, and 7203 expanded nodes at depths 2, 3, and 4, with 0, 312, and 1520 cache hits respectively.

At depth 2 delta computation made the combined engine 5.1 percent faster than the prior combined implementation, but there were still no transposition hits and it remained 30.7 percent slower than baseline.

At depth 3 delta computation made the combined engine 4.4 percent faster than the prior combined implementation. The engine retained a 44.47 percent expanded-node reduction but remained 60.7 percent slower than baseline.

At depth 4 delta computation made the combined engine 4.0 percent faster than the prior combined implementation. The engine retained a 56.83 percent expanded-node reduction and narrowed its runtime gap to 8.1 percent slower than baseline.

This is the closest the pruning-heavy combined engine has come to a wall-clock win while preserving Baseline A policy exactly. The remaining gap is now small enough that eliminating repeated parent score scans during ordering is a well-isolated next performance hypothesis.
No browser AI behavior has been changed. These remain benchmark engines until a search configuration earns promotion.
